Completed datasets from a fit with missing values

Source: R/imputed_data.R
imputed_data.Rd

Draws the response with its gaps filled in, one completed dataset per posterior draw. The observed entries are the data and are the same in every draw; only the cells that were not measured vary, which is how the uncertainty about them shows up.

Usage

imputed_data(fit, ndraws = 100, seed = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'stanimal_imputation'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

fit

A fit from lmm_animal or lm_phen_cov whose response had missing values.

ndraws

Number of completed datasets to draw, taken evenly across the kept draws.

seed

Optional seed for the draws that are simulated rather than read from the sampler. It only matters for a phenotypic fit; an animal fit's gaps are already parameters.

x

An object from imputed_data().

...

Unused; for method compatibility.

Value

An object of class stanimal_imputation: a list with Y (individuals by traits by draws, with draws last, as in fit_draws), the observed response it came from, the gaps as a data frame of individual and trait positions, and the trait names. print() reports the imputed value of each gap with its 95% interval.

Details

An animal fit's gaps are parameters, so each draw is already a draw from the posterior of the missing values and is reported as it is. A phenotypic fit has no such parameters – the missing values were integrated out – so each gap is drawn from the normal conditional distribution given that row's observed traits, using P and beta at the same draw. The two give the same kind of object, which is why one function covers both.

Use these for imputation-style follow-up analyses, or to see what the model believes about the cells it never saw. Do not collapse them to a single filled-in matrix and treat it as data: the spread across draws is the point.

See also

posterior_predictive, fit_loo

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
Y[c(2, 9), 1] <- NA
fit <- lmm_animal(Y, X, A)
imp <- imputed_data(fit, ndraws = 200)
imp                                   # each gap with its interval
dim(imp$Y)                            # individuals x traits x draws
} # }
